Control Objective: Ensure sensitive attributes and their close proxies do not drive Beacon outputs
Control Description: Before build freeze Credit Analytics documents every model feature and its source; confirms age; name; language and marital status are excluded; and tests FSA and employer for proxy strength against census-based demographics. Any retained high-proxy feature needs a documented AI Governance Committee decision
Evidence Produced: Feature register with sign-off; proxy analysis report; committee minutes for any retained feature
Testing Frequency: Annual and at each material model change
Test Procedure: Internal Audit compares the production feature list to the approved register and confirms every retained high-proxy feature has a dated committee decision
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.11; MAP 2.3 | ISO 42001 Annex A.7 | EU AI Act Art. 10(2) (benchmark) | Canadian human rights legislation (Legal to confirm grounds by province)

Control Objective: Detect differential outcomes before deployment when demographic data is not collected
Control Description: Credit Analytics runs pre-deployment fairness testing using three proxy methods: geographic analysis against census data; name-based analysis; and synthetic matched pairs that differ in one proxy attribute only. Model Risk Management challenges the results. Results are compared with thresholds set by the AI Governance Committee (OI-07). Methods and their limits are documented and results are never used to decide individual applications. Legal confirms the methods are lawful first (OI-09)
Evidence Produced: Fairness test report with methods; data; results and limitations; Model Risk Management challenge memo; Legal confirmation
Testing Frequency: Before pilot and before each rollout expansion
Test Procedure: Internal Audit re-runs the matched-pair test on a sample of files and reproduces the reported gap within a stated tolerance; confirms thresholds match committee minutes
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.11; MEASURE 2.1 | ISO 42001 Annex A.5 and A.6 | EU AI Act Art. 10(2); Art. 9 (benchmark)

Control Objective: Detect emerging fairness drift in live outcomes
Control Description: An automated report compares Standard Review; Enhanced Review and Recommend Decline rates for proxy-inferred groups against a reference group; weekly in pilot and monthly after. The 0.80 ratio is an investigation trigger only and not a legal standard. Each breach is logged and routed to the AI Governance Office with a disposition within 5 business days
Evidence Produced: Monthly fairness report; breach log with dispositions
Test Procedure: Internal Audit recomputes the ratios for one month from raw outcome data and confirms every breach has a logged disposition within 5 business days
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.11; MEASURE 2.4 | ISO 42001 Annex A.6 (operation and monitoring) | EU AI Act Art. 72 (benchmark) | OSFI E-23 monitoring expectations (confirm scope)

Control Objective: Provide independent challenge of soundness; performance and fairness before use
Control Description: Model Risk Management (second line) independently validates Beacon before pilot: conceptual soundness; out-of-time and segment performance; the reject inference approach; reason code behaviour; and the fairness results from CTL-02. Findings are rated and every high-rated finding must be closed before the approval gate
Evidence Produced: Validation report; findings log; closure evidence; approval gate minutes
Testing Frequency: Before pilot; annually; and on material change
Test Procedure: Internal Audit confirms the validator is independent of the developers and that every high-rated finding has closure evidence dated before the gate decision
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.3; MEASURE 2.5; MEASURE 2.11 | ISO 42001 Annex A.6 (verification and validation) | EU AI Act Art. 9; Art. 15 (benchmark) | OSFI E-23 validation and independent challenge (confirm scope)

Control Objective: Confirm real-world performance as repayment outcomes mature
Control Description: A quarterly backtest compares scores with realized repayment outcomes overall and by segment against the validation baseline and agreed tolerances. Outcomes lag 6 to 12 months so CTL-12 provides interim evidence. Breaches follow the escalation trigger in the register
Evidence Produced: Quarterly backtest report with segment results and tolerance comparison
Test Procedure: Internal Audit re-performs one quarterly backtest from source data and agrees the results to the report; confirms any breach was escalated
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.3; MEASURE 2.4 | ISO 42001 Annex A.6 | EU AI Act Art. 15; Art. 72 (benchmark) | OSFI E-23 ongoing monitoring (confirm scope)

Control Objective: Keep adjudicator judgement independent on the highest-risk path
Control Description: The Workbench requires a written rationale on every Recommend Decline file whether the adjudicator follows or overrides it and the rationale must cite file facts and not the score. The Human Oversight Framework (Artifact 6) lists mandatory override and escalation triggers such as a conflict between the summary and the source documents; the file cannot be completed until the adjudicator records a decision or escalates to a team lead
Evidence Produced: Workbench configuration record; rationale capture logs; escalation log
Test Procedure: Internal Audit tries to complete five test Recommend Decline files without a rationale and confirms the Workbench blocks completion; samples 25 live rationales for quality
Framework Mapping: NIST MAP 3.5; GOVERN 3.2 | ISO 42001 Annex A.9 | EU AI Act Art. 14(4) (benchmark)

Control Objective: Measure whether adjudicators reach sound decisions without seeing the recommendation
Control Description: A random sample of files (5 percent proposed as a starting rate) goes to blind re-review: the adjudicator decides before Beacon's recommendation is displayed. Blind decisions are compared with Beacon and with a senior reviewer panel and results feed CTL-08 and CTL-09
Evidence Produced: Sample selection log; blind versus assisted comparison; senior panel results
Test Procedure: Internal Audit re-draws the sample using the documented method and confirms selection was random and blind decisions were recorded before display
Framework Mapping: NIST MAP 3.5; MEASURE 2.4 | ISO 42001 Annex A.9 | EU AI Act Art. 14(4)(b) (benchmark)

Control Description: Workbench data feeds a report of concordance with Recommend Decline; override rate and median review time by adjudicator and team; weekly in pilot and monthly after. Team concordance above 90 percent in a month or an override rate below 3 percent triggers an AI Governance Office review and a tier reassessment. Both thresholds are starting values to calibrate against the pilot baseline
Evidence Produced: Concordance and override reports; escalation records; tier reassessment memos
Test Procedure: Internal Audit recomputes one month of concordance from Workbench logs and confirms each breach produced a reassessment record
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.4; MANAGE 4.1 | ISO 42001 Cl. 9.1 and Annex A.9 | EU AI Act Art. 14; Art. 26 (benchmark)

Control Objective: Ensure adjudicators understand model limits and keep independent skill
Control Description: Before getting Workbench access adjudicators complete training on Beacon's limits; automation bias and the mandatory override triggers. New adjudicators assess files before viewing Beacon during onboarding and everyone passes an annual manual-only competency check. Access is granted only after completion
Evidence Produced: Training content; completion records; competency check results; access provisioning records
Test Procedure: Internal Audit compares the Workbench user list with training completion records and confirms no user lacks a current completion
Framework Mapping: NIST GOVERN 2.2; MAP 3.5 | ISO 42001 Cl. 7.2 and 7.3 | EU AI Act Art. 4; Art. 14(4) (benchmark)

Control Objective: Ensure adjudicators and applicants can get accurate reasons for outcomes
Control Description: Independent validation tests whether the Review Priority Model reason codes and SHAP explanations reflect the factors that actually drive each score. Adverse-action notices must cite factors the adjudicator assessed on the file and must never cite the Beacon score alone. Legal concludes on whether applicants must be told AI is involved (OI-01; OI-09) and the decision is recorded
Evidence Produced: Reason code faithfulness section of the validation report; sampled adverse-action notices; Legal memo on applicant disclosure
Test Procedure: Internal Audit samples 25 adverse-action notices and confirms each cites adjudicator-assessed factors and none cites the score alone; confirms the validation report includes a reason code faithfulness test
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.8; MEASURE 2.9 | ISO 42001 Annex A.8 | EU AI Act Art. 13; Art. 86 (benchmark) | PIPEDA openness and individual access principles (Legal to confirm) | Provincial consumer credit notice rules (Legal to confirm)

Control Objective: Keep every LLM summary statement traceable to its source document
Control Description: The Summarization Assistant attaches a source document and page or field location to every figure and factual statement. The Workbench shows a link to the source and flags any statement without a valid citation. A monthly sample is checked for citation validity (98 percent proposed as a starting value). A month below the threshold disables LLM summarization through the feature flag pending review
Evidence Produced: Citation check logs; monthly sample audit results; feature flag change records
Test Procedure: Internal Audit draws 50 summaries from one month and verifies each citation points to the stated source location; confirms any month below 98 percent led to a feature flag action or a documented decision
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.5; MEASURE 2.8 | ISO 42001 Annex A.6 (verification and validation); Annex A.8 | EU AI Act Art. 13; Art. 15 (benchmark) | GenAI Profile risk: Confabulation

Control Objective: Detect score and input instability before outcome data is available
Control Description: An automated monthly report calculates Population Stability Index on the score and the top 10 features and tracks score distribution and review path mix by segment as early indicators. PSI of 0.10 is a watch level and 0.25 is an investigation level (common industry conventions used as starting values). Two consecutive months above 0.25 open a model review and notify Model Risk Management
Evidence Produced: Monthly monitoring report; alert and disposition log; model review records
Test Procedure: Internal Audit recomputes PSI for one month from raw data and agrees it to the report; confirms each threshold breach has a logged disposition
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.4; MANAGE 4.1 | ISO 42001 Cl. 9.1; Annex A.6 | EU AI Act Art. 72 (benchmark) | OSFI E-23 ongoing monitoring (confirm scope)

Control Objective: Retrain or redevelop only through a controlled and re-validated path
Control Description: Retraining triggers are documented before deployment: a PSI breach; a fairness threshold breach; a backtest breach; and the scheduled annual review. Any retrain is a material change that needs re-validation by Model Risk Management and a fresh fairness test (CTL-02) before release. Each retrain is also assessed for feedback loop effects because future training data will include outcomes that Beacon influenced
Evidence Produced: Retraining trigger register; change tickets; re-validation reports; fairness re-test results
Test Procedure: Internal Audit traces every model version released in the period to a change ticket; a re-validation report and a fairness re-test all dated before release
Framework Mapping: NIST MANAGE 4.1; MEASURE 2.4; GOVERN 1.4 | ISO 42001 Cl. 8.1; Cl. 10 | EU AI Act Art. 9; Art. 17 (benchmark) | OSFI E-23 model change and redevelopment (confirm scope)

Control Objective: Make oversight demonstrable with a complete and tamper-evident decision record
Control Description: For every file the Workbench records the model and prompt versions; the recommendation shown; the time it was displayed; the adjudicator decision; any rationale; and any escalation. The log is append-only and access controlled. A daily reconciliation compares files completed in the loan origination system with records in the log and any gap is investigated within 2 business days. Capture must be live before pilot (OI-06)
Evidence Produced: Log schema and access records; daily reconciliation reports; exception tickets
Test Procedure: Internal Audit picks 25 completed files and confirms each has a complete log record; tests that log entries cannot be edited or deleted by Workbench users or engineers without a separate approved change
Framework Mapping: NIST MAP 3.5; GOVERN 3.2 | ISO 42001 Annex A.6 (operation and monitoring) | EU AI Act Art. 12; Art. 14 (benchmark) | OSFI B-13 logging expectations (confirm scope and status)

Control Objective: Prevent oversight from failing under workload pressure or when logging fails
Control Description: Weekly reporting tracks median review time per file and queue backlog by team against the pre-pilot baseline. If the capture rate falls below 98 percent in a week or logging is unavailable for more than 24 hours the Workbench suspends the Recommend Decline display and notifies the AI Governance Office automatically. The display returns only after capture is restored and confirmed
Evidence Produced: Weekly capacity report; suspension event log; notification records
Test Procedure: Internal Audit simulates a logging outage in a test environment and confirms the Recommend Decline display is suspended and the AI Governance Office is notified within the stated time
Framework Mapping: NIST MAP 3.5; GOVERN 3.2; MANAGE 2.4 | ISO 42001 Annex A.9; Cl. 8.1 | EU AI Act Art. 12; Art. 14 (benchmark)

Control Objective: Ensure the LLM vendor cannot keep or reuse Northstar data
Control Description: Before pilot the vendor contract includes zero retention of prompts and outputs (or a Privacy-approved and documented exception); a prohibition on using Northstar data for training or evaluation; deletion with a certificate at exit; and Canadian-region processing. Northstar verifies the terms in operation through a configuration check at go-live and an annual vendor attestation or audit
Evidence Produced: Executed contract and addendum; configuration verification record; annual attestation or audit report
Test Procedure: Internal Audit agrees each required term to the executed contract; inspects the tenancy configuration record; and confirms the latest vendor attestation is dated within 12 months
Framework Mapping: NIST MANAGE 3.1; MEASURE 2.10 | ISO 42001 Annex A.10; Annex A.7 | EU AI Act Art. 25 (benchmark) | PIPEDA accountability and safeguards principles for third-party processing (Legal to confirm) | Law 25 (Quebec applicants excluded from pilot)

Control Objective: Send and keep only the personal information Beacon needs
Control Description: A pre-processing step sends the LLM only the documents and fields needed and masks identifiers such as SIN and full account numbers before sending. A scheduled scan of prompt logs looks for unmasked identifiers weekly in pilot and monthly after. Retention and deletion rules for scores; reason codes; prompts and summaries are set with Privacy (7 years assumed for scores and reason codes pending Privacy confirmation) and enforced by an automated deletion job
Evidence Produced: Masking rule specification; log scan reports; deletion job logs; retention schedule approved by Privacy
Test Procedure: Internal Audit submits five test files seeded with dummy identifiers and confirms they are masked in the vendor prompt; reviews one scan report; checks deletion job logs against the retention schedule
Framework Mapping: NIST MEASURE 2.10; MANAGE 3.1 | ISO 42001 Annex A.7 | EU AI Act Art. 10 (benchmark) | PIPEDA limiting use; retention and safeguards principles (Legal to confirm) | Law 25 destruction of information (Legal to confirm)

Control Objective: Confirm every use of personal information has a lawful basis and a defined purpose
Control Description: The Privacy Office completes a Privacy Impact Assessment before build freeze covering training data; inference data; adjudicator notes and LLM processing. Every Beacon data element gets a documented purpose and lawful basis. Legal decides whether consent wording and applicant notice must change (OI-01; OI-09). High-rated PIA findings must be closed before the approval gate. Quebec applicants stay excluded until the Law 25 review is complete
Evidence Produced: Signed PIA; data element register with purpose and lawful basis; Legal memo on consent and notice; gate minutes
Testing Frequency: At each lifecycle gate and annually
Test Procedure: Internal Audit samples 20 data elements from the model feature list and the prompts and traces each to the register; confirms no high-rated finding was open at the gate decision date
Framework Mapping: NIST GOVERN 1.1; MAP 4.1; MEASURE 2.10 | ISO 42001 Cl. 4.2; Annex A.7 | EU AI Act Art. 10(2) (benchmark) | PIPEDA consent and limiting-use principles (Legal to confirm) | Law 25 privacy impact assessment duty for Quebec (Legal to confirm)
